articles.title: Kyle Pitts gives Zachariah Branch a rookie welcome he will never forget
articles.standfirst: It was an introduction to one of the NFL's oldest newcomer traditions
articles.summary: It was an introduction to one of the NFL's oldest newcomer traditions
articles.body:
For Atlanta Falcons rookie Zachariah Branch, signing his first NFL contract was supposed to be one of the biggest financial milestones of his young life. Then came dinner. According to the account circulating Friday, Branch joined the Falcons' offense for a team dinner, only to discover that veteran tight end Kyle Pitts had handed him three separate checks totaling more than $30,000.

The rookie, who had only recently signed a four-year contract worth roughly $7 million, was reportedly left completely shell-shocked by the size of the bill. It was an introduction to one of the NFL's oldest, and sometimes most expensive, rookie traditions.

The Falcons selected Branch with the No. 79 overall pick in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Atlanta officially signed him to his rookie contract in May, with Over The Cap listing the deal at $7.056 million over four years, including $1.59 million in fully guaranteed money. So, yes, Branch is now an NFL player with a multimillion-dollar contract. But that doesn't necessarily make a $30,000-plus dinner bill any less jarring.

Branch has a lot of versatility and ability

The reported prank comes at an interesting moment for Branch , who has quickly become one of the more intriguing young pieces in Atlanta's offense. The Falcons see the former Georgia standout as much more than a traditional slot receiver. Head coach Kevin Stefanski has emphasized Branch's versatility, his ability to line up all over the formation and his value as a returner.

"He really has a great schematic fit, also a great personal fit for what we believe in and how hard he works," Stefanski said after the draft. "Just a player that you can really line up all over the field. "Branch's skill set makes the financial shock of his rookie dinner even more fitting. He is a player capable of turning relatively ordinary plays into explosive ones.

Daniel Jeremiah of NFL Network highlighted that trait during the draft process, describing Branch as a player at his best with the ball in his hands. His combination of elusiveness, long speed and return ability helped make him one of the more dynamic playmakers available in the middle rounds.

Branch is learning another part of being an NFL player

Branch's 2025 season at Georgia reinforced that evaluation. He finished with 81 catches for 811 yards and six touchdowns, while the Falcons noted that 78 percent of his receiving yardage came after the catch. More than 75 percent of his career snaps came from the slot, but Atlanta believes his versatility can allow him to move around the formation.

That versatility is part of the reason the Falcons were so enthusiastic about bringing him into the building. General manager Ian Cunningham also praised Branch's personality and work ethic after the draft. "You talk to him, you understand what he's about, how passionate he is about this game," Cunningham said. "He loves this game and he loves to be out there and working in practice."Now Branch is learning another part of being an NFL player : the locker-room culture.

And apparently, that culture can come with a very large check. The reported dinner bill also puts into perspective just how different the NFL financial world can be for a rookie. Branch's contract is worth more than $7 million, but that figure is spread across four seasons, and the actual cash flow is considerably different from the headline number.

Over The Cap lists Branch's 2026 cash payout at approximately $2.48 million and his 2026 salary-cap charge at roughly $1.28 million. That's still life-changing money. But seeing three checks totaling more than $30,000 land in front of you is another matter entirely. Especially when you're the rookie.

articles.title: Za'Darius Smith, an NFL star who signed with the Falcons after retiring, acknowledges that three of his relatives died after leaving the Eagles
articles.standfirst: Smith details the devastating family tragedy that forced him away from football
articles.summary: Smith details the devastating family tragedy that forced him away from football
articles.body:
Za’Darius Smith has revealed the heartbreaking circumstances behind his decision to walk away from the NFL during the 2025 season, explaining that he lost his mother, grandmother and father in the months following his sudden retirement from the Philadelphia Eagles.

The 33-year-old veteran pass rusher had signed a one-year deal with Philadelphia but appeared in only five games before stepping away from football.

Smith said the decision came after he received a call from his mother’s doctor, who told him she didn’t have much time left to live.

Smith informed the Eagles that he needed to leave, but the team was reluctant to let him go. With no other option available, he decided to retire so he could focus on his family.

His mother eventually died, and Smith was then forced to endure two more devastating losses. He revealed that his grandmother died after his mother, followed by the death of his father.

“Dealt with that. After losing my mom, I lost my grandma. Then after my grandma, I just lost my dad,” Smith told reporters, reflecting on an incredibly difficult period of his life.

The three-time Pro Bowl selection admitted that the losses left him in a very dark place. After spending months away from football, he gradually began to rediscover the joy that the game had once brought him.

Smith believes football can be his happy place again

Smith’s return began unexpectedly when Cleveland Browns general manager Andrew Berry contacted him earlier this month. Berry had previously worked with the veteran and initially checked in to see how he was doing before discussing the possibility of a comeback.

Smith eventually traveled to Cleveland for a workout. Although he didn’t reach an agreement with the Browns, the experience helped reignite his desire to play.

That ultimately led him to Atlanta, where the Falcons offered him a one-year, $6 million contract. The move also has a deeply personal connection for Smith because his late mother had always wanted him to play for Atlanta.

During his introductory press conference, Smith became emotional while explaining what football now means to him.

"My mom, rest her soul, man, she always wanted me to be in Atlanta with the Falcons,” said Smith .

For Smith , the move to Atalanta represents an opportunity to find happiness and purpose again rather than just extending his career.

The veteran has also given himself another professional target. Smith currently has 70.5 career sacks and wants to reach 100 before his career ends.

He’ll now attempt to pursue that milestone with his seventh NFL team. After previously playing for the Baltimore Ravens, Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings, Detroit Lions and Eagles, Smith is preparing for a new chapter with Atlanta.

His comeback comes after one of the most painful periods of his life, but Smith appears determined to make the most of the opportunity.
